extraction.name: MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI
extraction.description: A benchmark of 11.5K multimodal questions spanning 6 disciplines, 30 subjects, and 183 subfields, curated from college exams, quizzes, textbooks, online sources, and lecture materials to evaluate multimodal understanding and reasoning at college level.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
extraction.citeAs: MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark was manually curated in three stages: first, subjects were selected from common university majors based on whether visual inputs are commonly used; second, over 50 university students, including co-authors, collected multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources and created new questions when necessary; third, the authors cleaned the data by removing duplicates, checking format and typos, and assigning difficulty levels, excluding about 10% of very easy problems.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Document analysis, Web Scraping
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: College exams, quizzes, textbooks, online resources, and lecture materials; questions were also drawn from free online resources and study materials.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Potential duplicates were identified using lexical overlap and source URL similarity, then reviewed and removed by authors; problems were distributed among co-authors for format and typo checking; questions were categorized into very easy, easy, medium, and hard, and approximately 10% of very easy problems were excluded.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Questions were filtered to ensure they contained one or more images, were in English, were college-level, were unambiguous, and could be answered with one of the given options or a short answer; duplicate and very easy items were removed; standardized formatting was enforced.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Over 50 university students, including co-authors, acted as annotators to collect multimodal questions and create new ones when needed. They were instructed to follow copyright and license regulations, avoid sources prohibiting copying or redistribution, and select questions without immediately available answers. Authors later reviewed, cleaned, and categorized the questions by difficulty.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A user-friendly web interface for data annotation and verification was developed.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A secondary review team vetted annotations for quality and guideline adherence; regular audits of random samples were conducted; ambiguities were collaboratively reviewed in team meetings; questions were categorized by difficulty and some very easy items were excluded.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in the relevant majors; 90 college senior students were used as human experts for validation evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Versioned releases are documented in the version change log (V1 to V4), with updates including added model results, corrected typos, renamed models, and added human expert results. The dataset is maintained through benchmark updates and a live-updating leaderboard.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The protocol states that annotators should avoid collecting questions that contain any private information.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to monitor progress toward Expert AGI and is discussed in relation to potential job displacement and economic disruption from advanced AI systems.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The authors note that the manual curation process may carry biases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI because there is no direct mapping between MMMU performance and the 90th percentile of skilled adults, and college exams are not the only tasks an AGI should tackle. The manual curation process may carry biases, and the focus on college-level subjects may be insufficient for testing Expert AGI.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking, validation, and testing of multimodal models; zero-shot evaluation is emphasized, with some few-shot results reported in the appendix. The dataset includes development, validation, and test splits.
